transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-08 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Sasha Patel, Marcus Liu, Evelyn Park (Redwood); Aisha Rahman, Carlos Mendes, Priya Singh, Tom Becker (Novus Labs)

Summary (auto): Optimize walkthrough focused on quantization tradeoffs (INT8 vs FP8), quality vs latency benchmarking, recommended profiles for Novus' low-latency customer-facing summarization workload. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot benchmark.

Topics: quantization profiles, INT8 performance, FP8 quality, batching and latency SLOs, KV cache impacts, dedicated vs hosted routing, security and KMS concerns.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Sasha: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Sasha from Redwood, AE on the account, with Marcus our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Aisha: Good, thanks. Excited to see the quantization walkthrough — we've been tuning for latency and cost and kinda hit a wall.
[00:20] Marcus: Awesome. Quick agenda: run through INT8 vs FP8 profiles, show some quality vs latency charts, talk about tradeoffs for your summarization pipeline, and then next steps for a benchmark.
[00:31] Priya: Sounds good. Our main constraint is <200ms 95th percentile for short summaries, but cost can't triple.
[00:40] Marcus: Totally, that's what we'll focus on.
[00:45] [00:45] Marcus: Quick context question — what's your current deployment? Hosted or on-prem?
[00:50] Carlos: We're hybrid. Prod inference runs in our cloud VPC on k8s, some on dedicated GPU nodes. We want VPC/private options and eventual on-prem for regulatory customers.
[00:59] Marcus: Great, that maps to Redwood Dedicated or Private deploys. We'll call out config differences.
[01:10] Sasha: Marcus, why don't you kick us off with the INT8 profile overview?
[01:14] Marcus: Sure. So INT8 gives you big throughput gains, lower memory, lower cost. For many models we see ~2-3x token throughput improvements vs standard FP16 on the same hardware. The tradeoff is potential small quality regression on sensitive generation tasks. For summarization it's often acceptable, but depends on prompt sensitivity.
[01:35] Aisha: When you say quality regression, is that hallucination or phrasing differences?
[01:40] Marcus: Mostly phrasing differences, sometimes slightly lower fidelity on rare facts. Hallucination rates don't typically spike dramatically, but you'll see subtle changes. We recommend running a targeted eval set.
[01:50] Tom: Do you support per-layer mixed quant profiles? like keep first and last few layers higher precision?
[01:56] Marcus: Yes. We have hybrid profiles — e.g., INT8-mixed where attention/query/key layers stay in FP16 and intermediate MLPs are INT8. That gets most throughput with less quality loss.
[02:10] [02:10] Marcus: Next FP8 — it's a newer format. FP8 often preserves more of the model dynamics than INT8, so quality stays closer to FP16 while still improving throughput and memory, though not always as dramatic as INT8 in pure throughput. In practice FP8 is a nice midpoint.
[02:31] Priya: Any gotchas on hardware support?
[02:34] Marcus: FP8 requires specific kernels and runtime support; on NVIDIA Hopper/Ampere derived boxes we have optimized kernels. On older hardware FP8 might fall back to software and bring overhead. We'll highlight supported instance families in the benchmark report.
[02:48] Carlos: How about latency — do we see INT8 always faster tail latency, or sometimes batching changes that hurt p95?
[02:55] Marcus: Good question. For small prompt sizes, INT8 reduces per-token compute but batching strategy dominates latency. If you're doing single-request low-latency, kernel startup and memory transfer patterns matter. We recommend continuous batching plus prefix KV cache for multi-turn, and lower batch sizes with reserved capacity (Dedicated) for p95 SLOs.
[03:18] Aisha: Can you show those charts?
[03:20] Marcus: Yep, pulling up a chart — forgive the screen sharing lag.
[03:26] Marcus: Here's a quality vs latency scatter: x-axis p95 latency, y-axis rouge-f1 (we use a summarization eval). FP16 baseline sits at ~220ms p95 and rouge 0.78. INT8 mixed drops p95 to ~140ms and rouge 0.75; FP8 profile sits around 160ms and rouge 0.77. So depending on your threshold you pick FP8 for closer quality or INT8 for cost/latency.
[03:55] Priya: That half-point for FP8 looks compelling — small quality delta but decent latency gain.
[04:02] Marcus: Exactly. Also note quantization profiles vary by model architecture — decoder-only vs encoder-decoder have different sensitivity.
[04:14] Tom: You mentioned KV cache earlier, can you expand?
[04:18] Marcus: Sure — KV (key-value) cache lets you avoid recomputing prefixes; we sometimes see significant p95 improvements for dialog-like workloads. But cache eviction, memory footprint with INT8 vs FP8 needs consideration. INT8 reduces memory so cache capacity increases, which is good. Occasionally there are serialization/precision quirks with FP8 when resuming caches — we'll note that.
[04:45] Aisha: Security: if we run Dedicated in our VPC, how do keys and logs work? KMS integration?
[04:51] Sasha: Yes, Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS, HSM options through our Private offering. We also provide audit logs and can add retention controls. We'll send the SOC2/ISO docs.
[05:03] Carlos: Does quantization change how we need to handle PII? Any inference artifacts stored differently?
[05:09] Marcus: No change in data flow — quantization is model weights/storage/execution. Data-in-flight policies are the same; logs are configurable. We'll share our security appendix.
[05:19] [05:19] Marcus: Back to benchmarks — recommended approach: run parallel profiles against your evaluation set with realistic traffic. We'll instrument p50/p95, token cost, and qualitative diffs using your prompt set.
[05:34] Aisha: We can share a 2k prompt seed set and sample traffic distribution.
[05:38] Sasha: Great — action item for Aisha to share that. We'll then run a 2-week benchmark on Dedicated dev capacity or on-hosted with reserved capacity.
[05:49] Carlos: Pricing question — how much delta for Dedicated pilot?
[05:52] Sasha: We'll send a pilot pricing deck; it depends on nodes and reserved commit. For planning we gave a ballpark earlier but Marcus will include estimated token unit cost differences for INT8/FP8.
[06:05] Marcus: I'll also include a spreadsheet with throughput numbers per GPU SKU.
[06:11] [06:11] Aisha: Any recommended prompts tweaks for INT8? We worry about prompting tricks to stabilize outputs.
[06:18] Marcus: For INT8 we often advise slightly constrained decoding — lower temperature, higher top_p, and deterministic stopping tokens; those reduce variance in phrasing. We'll include a prompt-stability appendix.
[06:32] Priya: If we see quality regression in INT8, what's the rollback?
[06:36] Marcus: Redwood routing can fallback: you can circuit-break to FP16/FP8 variants for specific traffic slices while keeping bulk on INT8. Canary rollout by user cohort or route is recommended.
[06:48] Tom: How much engineering work to flip routes?
[06:51] Sasha: You can configure rollouts in Console; API calls include model variant flags and we have SDK examples. Marcus can show a snippet.
[06:58] Marcus: (shares code) Here's a simple policy config — route by path, percent traffic to variant. Most customers set up canary to 5% for a day then ramp.
[07:12] Aisha: Great.
[07:15] [07:15] Sasha: Quick notes on model selection: we recommend benchmark with the exact model + tokenizer you plan to serve. Sometimes quant tooling chooses different kernel variants which changes perf.
[07:26] Carlos: Curious if you support automatic quant profile suggestions?
[07:30] Marcus: Yes — Redwood Optimize has an auto-suggest that analyzes your eval and recommends profiles (INT8-mixed, FP8, etc.) with expected quality delta and cost savings. We'll include the suggestion output in the report.
[07:44] Aisha: How long to get the initial report?
[07:47] Sasha: Once you share the prompt set, Marcus can run an initial 3-day run and share a preliminary report, then a 2-week extended run for stability.
[07:56] Marcus: I'll scope the scripts and baseline today.
[07:59] [07:59] Priya: Any mention of competitors? We looked at Anthropic's hosted offering and OpenAI — how are Redwood's latency profiles different?
[08:08] Marcus: Public APIs are simple but usually don't expose dedicated reserved capacity or low-level kernel tuning. With Redwood Dedicated you control batching, reserved capacity, and get kernel-level optimizations which helps hit strict p95 SLOs. We'll call out direct comparisons in the benchmark appendix.
[08:26] Tom: A minor transcription hiccup — we sometimes saw "K V cash" in earlier notes — ignore that.
[08:31] Marcus: (laughs) fair.
[08:34] [08:34] Sasha: Ok let's recap and wrap: Next steps — Aisha shares the prompt set and traffic profile by May 12; Marcus kicks off the 2-week benchmark and shares a baseline scripts and preliminary 3-day results by May 15; Sasha will send SOC2 + pricing deck and Optimize guide by May 10.
[08:55] Aisha: That timeline works for us.
[08:58] Priya: Quick question — if we want per-tenant customization later, is that supported?
[09:03] Marcus: Yes — Multi-tenant routing with per-tenant profiles is supported in Console; we'll demo in a follow-up if you want.
[09:11] Sasha: Great — we'll set a follow-up to demo per-tenant rollouts.
[09:15] [09:15] Sasha: Any other blockers?
[09:18] Carlos: None from infra side — just the sample data and access for the benchmark.
[09:22] Aisha: No blockers.
[09:24] Sasha: Awesome. We'll send notes and the action items. Thanks everyone.
[09:30] (call ends)
